{{Quote|There goes another one.|Lieutenant Hija, to Gunnery Captain Bolvan|<ref name="ANH" />}}
'''Hija''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] who served as the [[chief gunnery officer]] of the [[Galactic Empire]]'s [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Devastator]]''. In the [[Standard year|year]] [[1 BBY]], he was onboard the ''Devastator'' following the [[Battle of Scarif]] when it pursued the fleeing [[CR90 corvette]] ''[[Tantive IV]]'', a [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] [[Starship|vessel]] carrying stolen [[Death Star plans|plans]] to the Imperial [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[superweapon]]. After the [[Star Destroyer]] caught up with the [[corvette]] and [[stormtrooper]]s successfully boarded the Alliance vessel, Hija was manning one of the ''Devastator's'' guns and noted an [[escape pod]] that had launched from the corvette, but was ordered not to shoot at it by [[gunnery captain]] [[Bolvan]]. The pod was carrying two Rebel [[droid]]s carrying the plans, and in order to cover up his mistake, Bolvan later put through an order that required Hija to take part in an inspection of the ''Devastator's'' weapons, keeping him out of the way so he could not be questioned.

==Biography==
{{Quote|As the gunnery captain, you are one of the few officers on board with enough authority to request such an action, and Imperial regulations require the chief gunnery officer to be in charge of the inspection. Hija will be occupied for the rest of the day climbing from gun embankment to gun embankment outside the ''Devastator''.|Arvira, to Bolvan|<ref name="TSOD">{{StoryCite|story=The Sith of Datawork|book=From a Certain Point of View}}</ref>}}
[[File:Bolvan-Hija-ANH.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Gunnery Captain Bolvan instructs Hija not to fire on the escape pod.]]
Hija<ref name="TSOD" /> was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] who served in the [[Imperial Navy]] of the [[Galactic Empire]] during the [[Galactic Civil War]] between the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] and the Empire.<ref name="ANH" /> In the [[Standard year|year]] [[1 BBY]],<ref name="Date">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas: Updated Edition]]'' dates the events of ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'' and prior to the [[Battle of Yavin]] in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']] to [[1 BBY]].</ref> he was stationed as a [[chief gunnery officer]] on board the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Devastator]]'', flagship of the [[Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]].<ref name="TSOD" /> In that year,<ref name="Date" /> the Alliance [[Battle of Scarif|attacked]] the Imperial [[Citadel Tower]] on the [[planet]] [[Scarif]] and managed to steal [[Death Star plans|plans]] to the Empire's [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[superweapon]]. The ''Devastator'' arrived at the climax of the battle, and gave chase when the Rebel<ref name="RO">''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''</ref> [[CR90 corvette]] ''[[Tantive IV]]''<ref name="USW">''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]''</ref> fled from Scarif carrying the plans.<ref name="RO" />

The ''Devastator'' caught up with the ''Tantive IV''<ref name="ANH" /> in the [[Tatoo system]],<ref name="USW" /> and there deployed [[stormtrooper]]s to board the Rebel vessel. During the boarding, Hija was manning one of the ''Devastator's'' guns<ref name="ANH" /> while sat next to [[Lieutenant]] [[Ciena Ree]]<ref name="Lost Stars">''[[Lost Stars]]''</ref> and witnessed several [[escape pod]]s launch from the ''Tantive IV''. One of these pods carried the Rebel [[droid]]s [[R2-D2]] and [[C-3PO]], who had been given the Death Star plans by [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]]; however, when Hija pointed the pod out,<ref name="ANH" /> his superior officer [[Gunnery captain|Gunnery Captain]] [[Bolvan]]<ref name="TSOD" /> ordered him not to shoot, as there was no readings of life signs on board<ref name="ANH" /> and Imperial regulations that tied gunnery officers' promotions to their kill ratios would label shooting an empty escape pod as a wasted shot.<ref name="TSOD" />

When the Death Star plans were not found on board the ''Tantive IV'', Bolvan realized they must have been in the escape pod and panicked, going to [[fleet logistics liaison]] [[Arvira]] to see if they could help him avoid the consequences of his mistake. Arvira agreed to help Bolvan, and as part of the cover-up they told him to fill out [[Form INS-776-TX]], which requested an immediate mid-cruise extra-vehicular-armament inspection. Such an inspection required the presence of the chief gunnery officer, and so Hija would have to join the inspection crew in climbing to each gun emplacement on the ''Devastator's'' exterior for the rest of the [[Standard day|day]] in order to comply. This kept Hija out of the way and prevented him from being questioned over Bolvan's orders concerning the escape pod.<ref name="TSOD" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|He's going to hate me. He never wants to go outside—says it gives him spacesickness—|Bolvan baulks at sending Hija onto the exterior of the ''Devastator''|<ref name="TSOD" />}}
Hija had [[Color|fair]] skin and brown [[hair]].<ref name="ANH" /> He claimed that going onto the exterior of starships while in [[Realspace|space]] gave him [[spacesickness]], and Bolvan believed that sending his subordinate onto the exterior of the ''Devastator'' would result in Hija hating him.<ref name="TSOD" />

==Equipment==
Hija wore a black [[Imperial military uniforms|Imperial officer's uniform]] with a [[Hat|cap]].<ref name="ANH" />

==Behind the scenes==
Hija was portrayed by [[John Wreford]]<ref name="ShowMaster">{{WebCite|url=https://showmastersonline.com/forums/index.php?/topic/81546-guest-announcement-john-wreford-star-wars-dr-who|text=Guest Announcement John Wreford Star wars, Dr Who|work=[http://showmasterssales.com Showmasters Comic Con Official Autograph Shop]|archivedate=20240723084857}}</ref> the film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], which was released on [[May 25]], [[1977]];<ref name="Year by Year">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, Updated and Expanded Edition]]''</ref> however, he first appeared in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization]] of the film written by [[Alan Dean Foster]]<ref name="Novelization">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novelization]]</ref> and released on [[November 12]], [[1976]].<ref name="Year by Year" /> Hija's name was first used in the novel,<ref name="Novelization" /> but not in the film,<ref name="ANH" /> and so it did not appear in [[canon]] until Hija was mentioned in the short story "[[The Sith of Datawork]]," which was written by [[Ken Liu]] and released as part of the ''[[From a Certain Point of View]]'' anthology book<ref name="TSOD" /> on [[October 3]], [[2017]].
